Six hands-on notebooks organised in two parallel tracks.

## Learn-the-Tool Track

Work through the measures in isolation, on controlled synthetic data where you
know the right answer, before touching real returns.

| Lab | Topic |
|-----|-------|
| [Tool 1 — The ladder](lab-tool1-ladder.qmd) | Pearson · Spearman · distance correlation |
| [Tool 2 — Information measures](lab-tool2-information.qmd) | Mutual information in bits · validating estimators |
| [Tool 3 — Windows](lab-tool3-windows.qmd) | Scalar → vector → block; total correlation |
| [Wrap-up — The Measure Zoo](lab-wrapup-zoo.qmd) | Every measure × every relationship shape, one benchmark grid |

## Do-the-Job Track

Task-shaped deliverables on real S&P 500 data (the 14-stock basket).

| Lab | Deliverable |
|-----|-------------|
| [Job A — Validate your tools](lab-jobA-validate.qmd) | Calibration sheet: every measure against a known answer |
| [Job B — The measure book](lab-jobB-measure-book.qmd) | Full pairwise dependence report for the basket |
| [Job C — Hidden risk](lab-jobC-hidden-risk.qmd) | Tail co-crash detection: the dependence that threatens a portfolio |

## Shared Setup

All labs load real data the same way:

```python
import sys, pathlib
sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path.cwd() / "src"))
from lectures import datasets, measures, plotting
from lectures.plotting import COOL, WARM, CRASH, INK, despine, annotate_box

import numpy as np
import einx                      # linear algebra with the axes spelled out
from jaxtyping import Float      # shape annotations: Float[Array, "n_days"]

Array = np.ndarray               # alias used in all shape annotations

R = datasets.load_returns()     # 14-stock daily returns DataFrame
META = datasets.load_basket_meta()
```

Two style conventions you will see in every snippet:

- **Shapes are documented**, e.g. `def f(z: Float[Array, "n_days"]) ->
  Float[Array, "n_days n_days"]` — you always know what goes in and out.
- **Linear algebra uses `einx`**, e.g. `einx.subtract("i, j -> i j", x, x)`
  instead of `x[:, None] - x[None, :]` — the axes are spelled out, not implied.
